sections.lead: We looked at your site the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Receiptable's name says receipt. Its headline says engagement.
sections.keep: The teal ribbon. It is a mark of its own and looks like nothing else in payments.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.what: The headline could sit on any loyalty or marketing tool.
pins.why: Engagement is the vaguest word in retail software, so it does not say why Receiptable and not the one next door.
pins.how: Name the receipt in the headline, since the receipt is what only Receiptable owns.
pins.label: Your headline
pins.cost: Buyers file it with every other tool that promises engagement.

pins.what: The one phrase that says what the product is sits in the pale grey subline.
pins.why: The name promises receipts. This is the only place the page talks about paper, and it is the quietest text on screen.
pins.how: Make the receipt the hero of the page and show one on screen.
pins.label: Your subline
pins.cost: The most ownable idea is a footnote.

pins.what: The logo strip sets Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay beside retail names.
pins.why: A reader cannot tell customers from payment methods, so the strongest social proof blurs.
pins.how: Show customers alone and say what each one does with Receiptable.
pins.label: Your logo strip
pins.cost: The proof reads as a list of payment logos.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at Receiptable. I spent some time on your site. Three things stood out, and they point the same way.
